questions.explanation: The distinction being tested is between what the view says and what critics fear. Moral anti-realism denies that moral claims describe objective mind-independent facts. This is the position defended by David Hume. The claim that moral anti-realism affirms objective moral facts is a common mistake about the view, often described as "realist misreading of anti-realism". A fair assessment also has to reckon with this worry: it may make moral disagreement puzzling. A careful reader separates the actual doctrine from the frequent misreading.
